mechanistic_insights: Self-driving laboratories accelerate discovery by using a closed-loop process where AI actively plans experiments based on prior results, reducing the number of experiments needed compared to high-throughput screening.

AI/ML algorithms can actively explore a candidate space by recommending experiments that are either predicted to have high performance (exploitation) or are in regions of high uncertainty (exploration).

The modularization of self-driving laboratories (e.g., control software, ML models, experimental units) via application program interfaces (APIs) is a key step toward expanding their applicability and reducing deployment barriers.
ML models trained on data from both successful and unsuccessful experiments show improved performance, highlighting the need for standardized databases that store all experimental outcomes.

Intelligent experiment planners can use heterogeneous feedback from multiple characterization methods (e.g., fast/crude and slow/precise) and learn the bias between them to make more cost-effective decisions.

quantitative_outcomes.notes: This paper is a high-level opinion/review article on the concept of 'self-driving laboratories', which integrate artificial intelligence (AI) with automated experimental platforms. It does not report on a specific chemical reaction or optimization study. Instead, it discusses the methodology, challenges, and future prospects of using closed-loop, AI-guided experimentation to accelerate materials and chemical discovery. Its relevance is high as it describes the framework for advanced reaction optimization.
